## Summary

A third-party confirmation tweet quoting Kieran Duff (@kieran__duff, status 2108591128303812954): Duff built a strategy via his "Claude funnel" — **zero modifications outside the original source** — described as "a specific edge for yen pairs (long & short)", claimed profitable on USDJPY, EURJPY, GBPJPY, AUDJPY and CADJPY. **Strategy clue: "research Gotobi Days."** SystematicEdge fed the clue into Claude himself: "works on all JPY pairs wtf", not yet tested on indices. Parameters: **none** (no tuned inputs), **ATR-based stop loss**. He closes (truncated) asking for more ideas in the same family.

## Why it matters

- **Gotobi is the rare seasonal with an economic mechanism.** Gotobi days (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 of each month) are Japanese corporate settlement/remittance dates driving recurring JPY demand flows — a documented calendar anomaly, unlike the mechanism-less weekday filter in [[2026-10-01-algojan-nq-monday-short]]. Under the hypothesis-first rule of [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]], this idea passes the gate most "seasonal tendency" backtests fail: there is a *why* before the code.
- **The workflow signal: clue → Claude → strategy, zero human edits, independently reproduced.** Duff publishes a clue, a third party runs the same funnel and confirms on five pairs. That's the LLM-assisted research loop working as advertised — and the exact genre Peter/Martin demand skepticism toward, so the confirmation is interesting *as a process demonstration* even before believing the edge.
- **The index test is the built-in falsification probe.** If the edge is truly Gotobi settlement flows, it is JPY-specific and should NOT transfer to indices. SystematicEdge hasn't run it yet; transfer to indices would suggest curve-fit, non-transfer would be consistent with the mechanism.
- **Skepticism gates:** "profitable" carries no metrics — no period, trade count, win rate, or PF (fewer numbers than even the algojan claim supplied); "works on all JPY pairs" is weaker than it sounds because JPY crosses are highly correlated — five pairs ≈ one clustered sample, not five independent confirmations; no test shown that performance concentrates around Gotobi dates vs. the rest of the month (the mechanism's direct fingerprint); ATR SL with "no parameters" still hides ATR period choices; photo unopened; text truncated. Capture as a mechanism-positive seasonal candidate and a process exemplar — not a replication target until the Gotobi-date concentration check exists.
